subject: Hospitality
title: Desert Hospitality and Bedouin Tradition
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Desert Hospitality and Bedouin Tradition.

hook.text: Bedouin tradition requires hosting any traveler for three days—no questions asked.

buildup.text: Desert Hospitality and Bedouin Tradition sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: After three days, the host may ask the guest's name and purpose. Before that, curiosity yields to duty.

twist.text: This code was pragmatic: refusing hospitality in the desert could mean death. Generosity was reciprocal insurance.

climax.text: Modern luxury desert resorts echo Bedouin values: unconditional welcome, abundant food, and shelter from the harsh environment.

punchline.text: Three days of shelter, no questions asked. Bedouin hospitality is survival made sacred.

quiz.question: Why does Bedouin tradition require hosting travelers?
options: In the desert, hospitality is survival—refusing could mean death for the traveler
